1.note: A sound play: הַגּוּף (the body) and הַנָּגוּף (the stricken one).

2.note: חֲבָרַיִךְ can be "your companions" or, as in Isa 47:9, 12, "your spells" (binding charms), which fits "bound". Perhaps also a play on the name Ḥever.

3.note: וְיִתְרָעוּ is read from רעע, "do harm"; from רעה it would be "keep company" (Prov 22:24). The next line has לוֹ; read here as לֹא ("and do not touch me"). The sense of the pair is uncertain.

4.note: From Judg 5:2 בִּפְרֹעַ פְּרָעוֹת, a phrase of uncertain sense there. Here read as "run wild, wrought havoc".

5.note: "Only one" is a biblical name for the soul (Ps 22:21, 35:17). Also in the Inclination's poem.

6.he: וּמִ- / מָּרָה סְעִי אוּלַי בְּמִתְקָה תַחֲנִי
6.note: מִמָּרָה is "from bitterness" and also "from Marah", the station of bitter waters made sweet (Exod 15:23-25); so "its sweetness".

7.note: בַּשֵּׂר may be a verb ("the Lord brings tidings") or an imperative ("Proclaim the Lord of the world"). נַעֲנָה is read as "afflicted" (Isa 53:7); "answered" is also possible. The rest of the poem is God's word to the soul.

8.he: זֶה נוֹשֵׁךְ וְזֶה מוֹשֵׁךְ. אוֹיָה לִי כִּי גַרְתִּי מֶשֶׁךְ
8.note: A rhyme play: נוֹשֵׁךְ (bites), מוֹשֵׁךְ (drags), and מֶשֶׁךְ (Meshech, Ps 120:5), which also suggests "dragging".

9.he: אוֹחִיל לְפֵרוּד אֹהֲבִי הַזַּךְ וְהָ- / רִאשֻוןֹ
9.note: לְפֵרוּד may be "in the parting from" or "for the parting (from the body)", that is, she hopes for death to return to her first Lover. The reading is uncertain.

10.note: רָעִיתִי read as "I grazed" (compare Song 6:3 הָרֹעֶה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים). It can also be pointed רַעְיָתִי, "my beloved": "a lily in the gardens of love, my beloved".

11.note: Literally "your grief and your calamity will be broken". It may mean that death ends grief too, or that grief and ruin will burst upon her. Uncertain.

12.note: פְּחִי read from פוח/נפח, "breathe, blow": no one will call the soul back to breathe life into the body.
